homily:
We often think of the life of faith as a steady climb—a long, slow ascent toward a peak where everything finally becomes clear. But the Scriptures today suggest something else. They suggest that the life of faith is more like a roadside. It is a place where we sit, where we wait, and where we sometimes find ourselves in the dark, listening for the sound of something—or someone—approaching. In the Gospel, we find a man sitting by the road in Jericho. He is blind. He is stationary. The world is moving around him, the crowd is surging forward, but he is fixed in one spot, defined by what he lacks. He is defined by his blindness, by his reliance on others, by the dust of the roadside.

Then he hears the sound. A commotion. People talking. He asks a simple, piercing question: 'What is happening?' And the answer he receives is the only answer that matters: 'Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.'

Think of the stillness of that moment. The man does not see the face of Jesus. He does not see the robes or the dust kicked up by the sandals of the disciples. He only hears the name. And in that name, he finds the courage to break the silence. He shouts. The crowd, perhaps embarrassed by his intensity or worried about the decorum of the procession, tells him to be quiet. But he will not be quiet. 'Son of David, have pity on me!' He is not asking for a lecture. He is not asking for a philosophical explanation of his condition. He is asking for the only thing that can change his reality: the gaze of the Savior.

There is a profound, quiet beauty in this. We all have our own Jericho. We all have those moments where we feel like we are sitting by the side of the road, watching the world move on without us. Maybe it is the silence in a house that used to be full of laughter. Maybe it is the ache of a heart that wonders where the joy has gone. We sit there, and we hear the world moving, and we wonder if the Lord is truly passing by, or if He has moved on to someone else, somewhere else. But the truth is, the Lord stops. He always stops. The Gospel tells us, 'Jesus stopped and ordered that he be brought to him.'

Benjamin knew this movement. He was a boy who loved the mechanics of things—the way a plane lifts off the runway, the way code creates a new world on a screen. He understood that things have a trajectory. He loved his 'con chim airlines'—his little dream of flight. And in his own life, he was always looking toward the horizon. He had that brilliant, curious mind that wanted to know how everything worked, how everything fit together. But more than that, he had a heart that was already tuned to the frequency of the Divine. He was a boy who understood that to live is to be in motion toward the One who created us.

Sometimes, we think we have to be perfect to approach Him. We think we have to have our lives perfectly ordered, like a well-written program or a perfectly balanced equation. But look at the man in the Gospel. He has nothing. He is a beggar. He is blind. And yet, when Jesus asks him, 'What do you want me to do for you?', he asks for the one thing that will allow him to see the truth of his own existence: 'Lord, please let me see.'

Alan and Thao, I know the weight of the silence. I know that after five months, the world expects you to be 'moving on,' but the heart does not move on. It only deepens. It only learns to carry the weight with more grace. But remember the dream of the ice cream? Remember the way Benjamin was simply there, waiting in line, paying his way, just being a son? That was not a trick of the mind. That was a glimpse of the reality that the blind man in Jericho finally saw. The reality that we are all, even now, standing in the presence of the Lord. The veil is thin. The distance is not as vast as we imagine. Benjamin is not 'gone' in the way the world understands absence. He is simply on the other side of the light, waiting for the rest of the family to catch up.

There is a temptation, when we are grieving, to think that we have lost our way, or that the 'lampstand' mentioned in the Book of Revelation has been removed from our house. We worry that we have lost the love we had at first, because the joy has been replaced by such a profound, heavy sorrow. But the Lord does not come to you to scold you for your grief. He comes to you as He came to the blind man. He comes to stop the procession, to stand in the middle of your life, and to ask you the same question: 'What do you want me to do for you?'

It is okay to answer that honestly. You can tell Him, 'Lord, I want to see him again.' You can tell Him, 'Lord, I want to feel the peace that he feels.' You can tell Him, 'Lord, it is too heavy.' He is not offended by your honesty. He is the one who wept at the tomb of Lazarus. He is the one who knows what it is to be human, to be vulnerable, to be broken. He is the one who, like a good friend, sits with you in the dust of the road.

Ryan, my dear brother, you are carrying a piece of your brother's legacy in your own heart. You were there in the Ferris wheel, you were there on the train, you were there for the sushi cake. Those moments are not just memories; they are the foundation of who you are. Ben loved you with a brotherly love that is rare and beautiful. That love is a seed. It is a tree planted by running water, as the Psalm says. Even when the winter comes, even when the leaves seem to fade, the roots are deep. Your brother's love for you is a part of the 'tree of life' that the Lord promises to those who are victorious. You are never walking alone, because the love that bound you together is a divine thing. It is eternal.

We must look at the world differently, just as the blind man did after he received his sight. He didn't just walk away; he followed Jesus. He gave glory to God. That is our task today. To give glory to God, not because the path is easy, but because the Lord is walking it with us. We give glory by remembering the sweetness of a boy who wanted to give his entire piggy bank to his uncle, not because he had to, but because his heart was so large it could not contain its own desire to help. That is the spirit of the Kingdom. That is the spirit of Benjamin.

To all of you who are watching, who are carrying your own heavy crosses, who are sitting in the dark of your own Jericho—do not be afraid to shout. Do not be afraid to tell the Lord that you are hurting. He is passing by. He is right there, in the silence of your prayer, in the ache of your longing. He is the one who holds the seven stars in His right hand. He is the one who walks in the midst of the lampstands. He has not forgotten you. He has not left you.

Carry this out the door today: you are not defined by your loss. You are defined by the love that God has for you, a love that is stronger than death, a love that is waiting for you in the light. When you feel the sorrow, let it be a reminder that you have loved deeply, and that is the greatest sign of the divine within you. Benjamin is safe. He is home. And you, too, are being led home, step by step, through the grace of the One who makes the blind see and the weary find rest. Trust Him. Just trust Him. He is the light, and He is the way, and He is holding you, and your boy, in the palm of His hand.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

readings.label: Atuagak 1
readings.text: Ataniup takujaqtuutinga Jesus Christ, God-mit tunijaujuq, inuusiup iluani kikkutuinnarnut takujaujut. Ataniup uqalaurtuq angilikkut John-mut, taanna uqausiq tunijaujuq. Nalligijaujut taakkua atuqtuut, uqalautikkut, naalaqtutlu. John, taakkua arvinillit-atausirmit ilagiit Asia-mi: asanniniq qanuingittuq, Ataniup tunijanga. Ataniup uqausinga: 'To the angel of the Church in Ephesus, write this: The one who holds the seven stars in his right hand and walks in the midst of the seven gold lampstands says this: I know your works, your labor, and your endurance. Yet I hold this against you: you have lost the love you had at first. Realize how far you have fallen. Repent, and do the works you did at first. Otherwise, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.'

readings.label: Psalm
readings.text: R. Those who are victorious I will feed from the tree of life. Blessed the man who follows not the counsel of the wicked. Nor walks in the way of sinners, nor sits in the company of the insolent. But delights in the law of the LORD and meditates on his law day and night. R. Those who are victorious I will feed from the tree of life. He is like a tree planted near running water, That yields its fruit in due season, and whose leaves never fade. Whatever he does, prospers. R. Those who are victorious I will feed from the tree of life. Not so the wicked, not so; they are like chaff which the wind drives away. For the LORD watches over the way of the just, but the way of the wicked vanishes. R. Those who are victorious I will feed from the tree of life.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: Jesus Jericho-mut qanittuq, takujungittuq inuk inuusiup iluani. 'Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.' Taanna inuk nipiliuqtuq: 'Jesus, Son of David, have pity on me!' Kikkut uqalautikkut nipiliktaujut, kihiani taanna inuk nipiliuqtuq. Jesus aniguqtuq, uqaqtuq: 'What do you want me to do for you?' Taanna inuk uqaqtuq: 'Lord, please let me see.' Jesus uqaqtuq: 'Have sight; your faith has saved you.' Taanna inuk takulirpuq, Ataniup quviasungnirlugu.

pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
